# Spec Kit Delivery v1

Build the user-approved standalone private extension for Codex and Spec Kit 1.0.12.

- FR-001: Map requirements, acceptance criteria, and tasks to an approved baseline.
- FR-002: Execute CLI, API, UI, and inspection scenarios with observable assertions.
- FR-003: Preserve failed attempts, bound repairs to three cycles, and reject stale evidence.
- FR-004: Generate L0/L1/L2 browser and editable PowerPoint presentations from one source.
- FR-005: Require separate human GitHub approval and protected CI for final acceptance.
- FR-006: Install independently and alongside Agentstandards without changing its architecture gate.

- AC-001: Missing, duplicate, modified, skipped, and failed evidence cannot pass verification.
- AC-002: CLI, API, UI, and inspection success/failure fixtures exercise real execution.
- AC-003: Browser and PowerPoint preserve content, evidence links, images and speaker notes.
- AC-004: Agent, stale, dismissed, or unauthorized reviews cannot approve completion.
- AC-005: Clean Spec Kit 1.0.12 installation exposes all six commands and the wrapping preset.
- AC-006: No v1 completion claim until this repository has passed real human acceptance.
documents.plan.md:
# Approved implementation direction

The user approved the Spec Kit Delivery plan in this conversation on 2026-09-26.
This records implementation authorization, not a fabricated GitHub baseline approval.

Use a deterministic Python CLI, strict versioned schemas, Git/source fingerprints, and append-only
baseline/run directories. Execute project commands with timeouts, HTTP checks with httpx, UI checks
with Playwright, and text inspections against repository files. Use a shared presentation content
model for HTML and editable PowerPoint export. Keep generated evidence outside source control.

Read human authority from live GitHub APIs and trusted default-branch policy. Separate agent
barthisagent from human approver bbjwz. Keep privileged auditing on the default branch and never
execute candidate code in that job. Use the unprivileged review event only as a wake-up signal.

Bootstrap the private repo with user-approved initial README, then use draft PRs. Protection support,
reviewed runner pin, protected audit environment, and real human reviews are external activation
requirements. Missing requirements keep delivery unaccepted. No automatic merge or deployment.
